prior.notes:
Verdict: partly-new. Each ingredient has prior art, but the specific combination in the proposal (checker-safe one-step variants of a deployed stuck task, built in the same tool sandbox, minimal-criterion filter, same-world stones shown at test time, downstream-credit operator bandit, nightly LoRA climbing the frontier) did not appear in any 2023-2026 source found.

Overlaps by ingredient:
- Easier-variant generation with a verifier, then RL, and test-time variant trees: LADDER (2503.00735). This is the closest match and the proposal already names it. The 'tool sandbox + same-world stones + code-only check-relax/world-shrink operators + minimal criterion + downstream credit + frontier-tracking sleep' are the additions. LADDER-TTRL is the strongest prior for the per-task tree.
- Stepping stones / subproblems before solving: ARQ (2602.19069). Show a generated stone, then solve. Reasoning QA only; no tools, no checks, no retained-if-learnable filter. Its fine-tuned stone-writer is close to the proposal's optional DPO morph-writer idea.
- Minimal criterion / impossible-task filtering in LLM co-evolution: AC/DC (2604.14969), citing Brant & Stanley 2017 and Soros & Stanley 2014 (the 'arms race gives no signal' point). Supports the minimal-criterion step and the 'replace unsolved with parent' rule, which is a useful design precedent.
- Self-play curricula for tool agents: Agent0 (2511.16043), Tool-R0 (2602.21320), Self-Challenging (2025). Generate tasks from scratch; no anchor to a stuck real task.
- Hard-sample generation from tool failures: 'From Failure to Mastery' (2601.01498). Method not confirmed.
- Hindsight relabeling of agent trajectories: AgentHER (2603.21357, already known), Hindsight Supervised Learning (ICLR 2026, no id found). Proposal already distinguishes itself from these.
- Pure self-play stalls: R-Zero and Tool-R0 note marginal gains and degradation over iterations, relevant to the frontier-tracking claim. Socratic-Zero (2509.24726) argues prior self-play lacks quality control, which is the gap the minimal-criterion step targets.

Known-ids check: AgentHER 2603.21357 and AdaPT-style items 2510.04618 (ACE) and 2604.04804 (SkillX) are already known. The new candidates above (2503.00735, 2602.19069, 2604.14969, 2511.16043, 2602.21320, 2601.01498, 2509.24726, 2604.03472, 2605.23067, 2410.08632, 2607.04235, 2607.02599, 2607.16961) are NOT in known-ids.txt (grep count 0) and should be added if the sweep adopts them. Note: Vocabulary Dropout (2604.03472) and Skill Self-Play (2607.22529) also surfaced, the latter with a solve-rate frontier proposer; neither is a near match.

Test implications for the LADDER-1 plan: The 'ML > ML-noSol' and 'ML > R+' arms are the key novelty tests; LADDER is the baseline the proposal must beat, so the proposal should cite LADDER and ARQ explicitly and compare against a 'LADDER-style numeric-verifier-free' arm if possible. The 'shrink world / drop check' operators have no direct precedent found; this is the most likely novel piece.

Limits: 6 web searches, 0 page fetches used. Paper bodies were not read; claims come from search snippets. The 2025 'Hindsight Supervised Learning' and any 2026 papers on minimal-criterion LLM agents were not located. Not checked: OpenReview/ICLR 2026 listings beyond the one ICLR hit; GitHub."

fixable_flaws: Missing control (suggested, likely the biggest issue): a RELAX or SPLIT sibling is T minus its hardest check. Its solved transcript probably repeats what T's best failed try already did, because failed tries usually pass the easy checks. R+ as written shows failed tries, but probably not which checks passed or the highest-scoring partial try. So 'ML > R+' could mean 'per-check partial credit helps' and not 'climbing helps'. Fix: add an R+check arm with the same R+ block plus per-check pass/fail plus the 2 best partial tries on T, labelled the same way and token-matched. The real novelty test is ML vs R+check, not ML vs R+ or ML vs ML-noSol.

Unaudited HARD set (untested): a task can be 0/64 because the task or checker is broken, the spec is ambiguous, or a check reads reply wording. No ladder fixes those, and they lower every arm's ceiling. Before Stage A, label each HARD task as solvable or not, using a reference solution or one Claude Batches attempt per task with the harness checking it (this is grading and data, not a test-bed API dependency). Score only the solvable ones. I could not check the prerequisite: the Reach-1 task JSON, check lists, world items and reply checks are not in /home/user/learner (only mechanism/invent1_workflow.json mentions Reach-1).

Too many changes at once: Stage A changes the operator family (3 code + 4 model-written), the MC filter, the climb context, the Thompson credit table and the self-checks together. Run the code-only operators (RELAX/SHRINK/SPLIT, real checks, no self-check risk) as Stage A1. Add the model-written operators as A2 only if A1 passes. Model-written SWAP/INVERT self-checks can be trivially satisfiable, and the audit only measures that after budget has been spent.

Credit table cannot learn at this scale (suggested): 7 operators x 5 failure signatures = 35 cells, fed by at most a handful of downstream cracks. Thompson sampling will just be its prior. ML-T should be dropped from v1, not just made report-only, and the budget moved to seeds.

Unknown minimal-criterion yield: SHRINK keeps every check, so on a 0/64 task most SHRINK children will score 0/8. Many RELAX children will score 8/8 (the dropped check was the only one failing) or 0/8. Measure yield first: the share of HARD tasks with at least one sibling at 1-6/8. If it is low, the whole method is starved. A SHRINK crack is also a diagnosis in itself (distractors were the cause), which points to a retrieval or filter tool rather than a ladder.

Statistics too weak: with HARD split train/test, the test half is probably 15-30 tasks. 'ML − R+ ≥ 3' with discordant pairs at 3:0 has a two-sided McNemar exact p of about 0.25. Require replication on a second seed, or a discordant count of at least 5:1 over both seeds combined.

Stage B is a composition bet, and composition and hindsight relabelling both failed on the puzzle model (shown there, but on a different system, so only suggestive here). Training on 'first sub-goal' and 'one check dropped' wins and hoping greedy then solves the whole task is exactly that bet. Stage B should require that Stage A pass, not 'pass or inconclusive'. It should also add a check that the frontier actually moves: night-2 siblings must be measurably closer to T (fewer checks dropped) than night-1 siblings, or the claim that 'the ladder moves back toward the original' is unsupported.

Real-use fit is overstated: RELAX/SHRINK/SPLIT need a list of end-state checks you can drop. Ben's real stuck tasks ('that's wrong', a repeated tool error) usually have none. The mechanism transfers mainly to tasks with tests (code with a test suite, file outputs with a validator). Say so, and give real use a fallback: SPLIT by the model's own plan steps, with harness-checked read-only probes.
attack.fair_baseline: The fair baseline is R+check with tokens matched to ML, counting every morph call, sibling try and climb try. R+check means R+ (retries that see failed tries) plus, for each failed try on T, which checks it passed and failed, plus the 2 highest-partial-credit failed transcripts on T labelled as stepping stones in the same slot ML uses for solved siblings. Keep plain R+ and ML-noSol as secondary controls. For Stage B, the fair baseline is STaR on R+check wins on the originals, plus partial-credit trajectories (the best partial try per task, trained only on its passed-check prefix), with the same replay and KL anchor. A baseline that gets no partial signal at all would be unfairly weak.
attack.likely_effect: SUGGESTED: Stage A with code-only operators cracks a few HARD tasks (about 2-5 of a ~20-30 task test half) more than plain R+. The gap over R+check is probably 0-2, inside noise, because RELAX/SPLIT stones mostly carry the partial-credit information R+check already gives. SUGGESTED: SHRINK is the most likely to beat R+check where it works, because it removes distractor confusion that no retry block can, but its yield is likely low. UNTESTED: model-written SWAP/INVERT/PROBE stones. They could add real new information (a same-world worked example on another entity), but have the highest risk of a self-check passing while the real check would fail. UNTESTED, with a negative prior from the puzzle model's composition and hindsight failures (shown there, not here): Stage B moving greedy first-try on the originals by 4 or more. My expectation is 0-2 greedy cracks, with the gain appearing only in pass@8 with climb context. SHOWN: nothing yet. Reach-1 and its task schema are not in this repo, so the RELAX/SHRINK/SPLIT prerequisite is unverified.
attack.improved_test:
LADDER-0/A1, one change at a time. Pass marks are fixed now. Runs on the 5070 Ti after ~14:00Z Oct 26: about 1.5 h, no Vast.

STEP 0, AUDIT (about 20 min plus 1 Claude batch, report-only gates):
(a) Confirm that the task JSON exposes a list of droppable checks and world items, and whether any check reads reply text. If RELAX/SHRINK/SPLIT cannot be written in code, stop: the method is void as specified.
(b) Mark each HARD task solvable or not, using a reference solution or one Claude Batches attempt checked by the harness. Score only the solvable ones; report how many are unsolvable.
(c) From the existing 64 failed tries, record per-check pass rates per task, and list tasks where some failed try already passes every check except one.

STEP 1, YIELD (code operators only):
- Make every RELAX/SHRINK/SPLIT sibling, at most 6 per task.
- Run 8 tries each.
- Pass mark: at least 50% of solvable HARD tasks get at least one sibling at 1-6/8.
- Proved wrong: under 25%, which kills the method on Reach-1.
- Report yield by operator. Separately, any sibling that solves T outright (SHRINK keeps all checks) is a distractor diagnosis, not a ladder win.

STEP 2, A1 ARMS on the solvable HARD tasks:
- Use all of them. There is no credit table, so no train/test split is needed.
- Token-matched, counting every sibling and morph token. The R arms get extra T tries up to the ML total, cap 28.
- Arms:
  - R+
  - R+check (per-check results plus the 2 best partial T tries as stones)
  - ML-code (solved code siblings as stones, uniform operators)
  - ML-noSol
- 2 seeds.
- PASS: ML-code cracks at least 5 tasks pooled over both seeds; ML-code beats R+check with discordant pairs at least 5:1 pooled and the gain present in both seeds; ML-code beats ML-noSol by at least 2; at least 2/3 of wins replay with the same stones.
- PROVED WRONG: ML-code ≤ R+check, meaning the partial-credit information explains the gain and climbing adds nothing.
- INCONCLUSIVE: a gap of 1-2, or a gain in only one seed.

Only if A1 passes:
- A2 adds model-written operators. It is judged on its marginal gain over ML-code, with the self-check-vs-real-check audit run before any scoring.
- Stage B follows A2, and only if A2 passes, not if it is inconclusive. Its baseline is STaR on R+check wins plus passed-check prefixes.
- Stage B adds a frontier gate: by night 2, the median sibling must be at least 1 check closer to T than on night 1.
- Stage B keeps the plan's greedy-without-context pass mark.

The small card or puzzle results are only a prior here. They count as evidence for neither stage.

candidates.name: Doubt Forks: force the runner-up at the model's confident decisions, and learn which confidences to doubt
candidates.one_line: Find the decision tokens in a failed attempt where the model was nearly certain (above 0.9) but a second option still had real weight. Force that second option, continue in the replayed sandbox, learn with a small probe which kinds of confident point are worth doubting, and train on one-token-diff preference pairs so the find becomes the greedy first try.
candidates.mechanism:
DAY (stuck mode): start from the 2 failed transcripts R+ sees. (1) One teacher-forced prefill pass per transcript records the top-2 probabilities and the layer-L hidden state (L about 2/3 depth) at each assistant token. (2) Candidate forks are decision tokens only: the first token of each assistant turn (act or ask), the first token of a tool name, and the first token of each argument value. A candidate is kept if p1 ≥ 0.9 and p2 ≥ 0.005. The hypothesis (untested) is that confident but not certain choices are where unspoken assumptions sit, the reverse of the usual high-entropy forking-token view. (3) Ranking. v0 is a heuristic: log p2 plus a per-type weight. v1 is a learned logistic probe on the hidden state (about 3k parameters) that predicts P(the forked continuation succeeds). (4) Choose the top 16 forks, at most 3 per 50-token window. Rebuild the world by replaying the prefix's tool calls (the sandbox is deterministic), truncate the KV cache at the fork, force the runner-up token or tool, then sample at temp 0.7 under the 6-turn cap. (5) Wins are replayed 3× from the same fork and logged with fork type, position and the alternative token.
NIGHT: (a) Refit the probe on all fork outcomes so far, so the system learns which doubts pay. (b) Fork-DPO: chosen = the winning continuation from the fork, rejected = the original failed continuation from the same point. Because they share a prefix, the preference signal sits exactly on the forked decision. LoRA, beta 0.1, with the nightly KL anchor. (c) Each win becomes a card ('in jobs like X, don't assume Y, do Z') built from the token diff plus a one-line model summary, used only after Ben confirms it. PARTS: frozen backbone, a linear probe, the nightly LoRA. No second model.
candidates.why_fantastic: A model mostly cannot name the assumption it is blind to, which is why FLIP's 'opposites' collapse onto ask-vs-act. Doubt Forks reads those assumptions from the model's own probabilities. A near-certain choice with a live alternative is, mechanically, a premise it never examined. That turns 'think differently' into a search the model can carry out over its own commitments. It is the candidate most directly aimed at the measured greedy bottleneck (on the puzzle model, search finds fits for about 36 of 205 pool questions by night 4 while greedy first-try stays near 0). The training pairs differ at the exact token where greedy went wrong, so a search find can become a first-try habit. The probe gives the creative mode a skill that grows each night instead of a fixed prompt.
candidates.why_new: Not FLIP (a verbal listing; this uses logprobs and no listing prompt). Not R+ or a temperature change (this forces specific runner-up tokens at chosen points). Not PivoARL (2607.03702: one erroneous turn found by self-reflection). Not the forking-token / high-entropy-minority work (2412.07961, 2506.01939), which targets uncertain tokens; this targets confident ones and learns a probe for them. Shared-prefix fork-DPO is not the queued whole-reply DPO/KTO correction pairs. Branch-at-decode is on the map as UNTESTED and is not queued.
candidates.k2_test:
DF-1, shared K2 HARD screen, HARD split by task id into HARD-train and HARD-test. ARMS on HARD-test, temp 0.7: R+ (2 failed transcripts plus 'try a different approach'; extra tries until generated tokens match DF0, cap 24). DF0 (heuristic forks, 16). DF-rand (16 forks at random assistant tokens with p2 ≥ 0.005 and the same forcing: tests whether 'confident decision point' matters or any jolt would do). DF1 (probe trained only on HARD-train plus the 1-4/64 fork outcomes). Tokens-matched decides; tries-matched is also reported.
PASS (fixed): P1 DF0 cracks ≥5. P2 DF0 − R+ ≥ 3 and only-DF0 ≥ 2× only-R+. P3 DF0 − DF-rand ≥ 2. P4 each win replays ≥2/3 from its fork. P5 (night, only if P1-P2 pass): after 1 night of fork-DPO, greedy first-try solves ≥50% of the cracked tasks (base about 0), with no drop over 2 points on the 100 held-out tasks at greedy (paired McNemar). Bonus: DF1 − DF0 ≥ 2.
PROVED WRONG: DF0 ≤ R+ (tokens-matched), or DF0 ≤ DF-rand (plain perturbation, so the hidden-assumption story is false). 2-4 cracks or a gap of 1-2 is inconclusive: seed 2. Report wins by fork type; if over 70% are act/ask flips, record that it mostly re-finds the ask-vs-act default.
candidates.mac_fit: Fits. K2 q4 in mlx_lm; the teacher-forced pass over 2 transcripts of about 3k tokens is one prefill, under 1 s on the M1 Pro. Plain attention lets the KV cache be truncated at the fork. On the Qwen3.6 Gated DeltaNet tier this would need recurrent-state snapshots at decision tokens, so start on K2 only. The probe is a dot product on one layer, which needs a small hook in the mlx forward pass. Live budget: 8 forks × about 300 tokens within 30 s; the full 16 at night. Runs on the 8 GB M2. Fork-DPO trains at night on the PC or Kaggle, or slowly with mlx-lm LoRA.
candidates.test_cost: Estimated: the shared screen, then about 2,500 arm episodes (about 1 GPU-hour on the 5070 Ti), probe fitting in CPU-minutes, fork-DPO on a few hundred pairs in under 30 min. About 3 GPU-hours on the PC beyond nothing else, or about 6 on the second Kaggle T4x2 account. No API.

Prior-art check for Doubt Forks. Verdict: partly-new. Each component has precedent; the specific combination (near-certain tokens with a live runner-up, forced at decision tokens, ranked by a learned probe, then trained as shared-prefix fork pairs) did not appear in any search.

2. The "confident but not certain" framing is new relative to the forking-token papers, which target high entropy. The 2604.22271 paper (April 2026) argues that under greedy decoding the chosen token always looks maximally confident, so confidence alone may not localise errors. The candidate should test this directly against DF-rand.
3. The probe is close to ThoughtProbe and DUCHESS. Its novelty rests on applying the probe to ranking forced forks in the creative mode, not on the probe itself.

Search coverage: 7 web searches and 1 fetch used. Nothing found on forced runner-up tokens at confident decision points in agent trajectories with replay. fatal_flaws: None fatal as designed, but the night step (P5) cannot work as specified. It trains fork-DPO on cracks from HARD-test, then measures greedy first-try on those same cracked tasks. A 50% pass there would only show the model memorised a handful of task-specific token diffs, not a new first-try habit. On the puzzle model, hindsight relabel and composition already failed in the same way (shown on puzzles, untested on Reach-1). As written, P5 cannot tell memorising apart from learning, so it proves nothing about the main claim ('a search find becomes a first-try habit').

DF-rand is a strawman control, and P3 depends on it. 'Random assistant tokens with p2 >= 0.005' mostly lands in the middle of words, inside JSON punctuation, or in prose, where a forced token is usually either harmless or fatal. DF0 beating that only shows that decision tokens matter more than random tokens, which nobody doubts. It does not show that confident decision points hide assumptions. The 'reverse of the high-entropy forking-token view' story needs two controls that are missing: (a) forcing at high-entropy decision tokens (the 2506.01939 view), and (b) resampling without forcing at the same confident positions (is it the forced token or just the restart point?). Without them, P3 passing would be read as support for a story it never tested.
fixable_flaws: Tokenization aliasing (suggested, very likely): the runner-up at 'first token of a tool name' or 'first token of an argument value' is often a different spelling of the same thing: a leading space vs none, a quote vs no quote, 'read' vs 'read_' (a prefix of the same tool), a casing variant. Forcing it then completes the same action. Fix: greedy-complete the span after each candidate fork and keep it only if the decoded tool name or argument value differs semantically from the original. Report how many raw candidates survive this filter.

Supply risk (untested): with p1 >= 0.9 and p2 >= 0.005 restricted to decision tokens, 2 transcripts with at most 6 turns may contain far fewer than 16 qualifying forks. Say what fills the shortfall. If it is lower-ranked forks, DF0 slowly turns into DF-rand. Measure candidates per task offline first, on the 270 paused Reach-1 episodes and the existing HARD failure transcripts, with no GPU needed.

The probe (DF1) has almost no data. 1-4/64 positive fork outcomes on HARD-train means a few dozen positives at most, for about 3k parameters on a ~2/3-depth hidden state. It will overfit, and 'DF1 − DF0 >= 2' is noise at this N. Drop DF1 from the first test. Reintroduce it only after there are at least 30 positive fork outcomes, and judge it by held-out AUC against the heuristic, not by cracks.

Sample size is not stated. P1 'cracks >= 5' and P2 'gap >= 3' mean nothing without the number of HARD-test tasks. With about 30 HARD-test tasks and base rates near 0, a gap of 3 is within seed noise. State N, pre-register a paired per-task sign test on only-DF vs only-R+, and size the screen so HARD-test has at least 40 tasks.

Token matching hides work. DF arms reuse the prefix (KV cache plus replayed tool calls), so they generate fewer tokens per try but process the full prefix again. That is fair on generated tokens but not on wall-clock time or prefill FLOPs on the Mac. Report wall-clock per arm on the M1 Pro as a third axis, since the live budget is about 30 s.

Replay determinism is assumed, not checked (untested). Even if the RLAIF sandbox checks are deterministic, tool outputs that include timestamps, random ids or ordering will make the replayed world differ from the original. Before the arm run, add a replay-equality check that hashes every replayed tool output against the original transcript.

Fork-DPO with beta 0.1 on a few hundred one-token-diff pairs is close to a token-level SFT push, and could make that token over-preferred everywhere (for example 'always ask first'). The fixed 'no drop over 2 points on the 100 held-out tasks' guard is good. Add a per-fork-type check of how often the forced token's greedy rate rises on held-out tasks where it is wrong.

The prior-art notes should be fixed in the card. 2412.07961 is unverified (cite 2506.01939 alone). 2606.23112 already does divergence-point DPO for tool agents, so the only new part of the night step is that the alternative is forced by logprob rather than taken from a rollout. 2604.22271 argues that confidence alone may not localise errors. That is the hypothesis to test, not a footnote.

Real-use fit is narrower than claimed. Ben's real tasks (files, web, mail, school) are not deterministic to replay, and tool calls with side effects cannot be re-run up to the fork. Live use therefore needs either sandboxed or cached tool outputs, or forks only before the first side-effecting call. The Qwen3.6 Gated DeltaNet tier needs state snapshots that do not exist yet. Treat it as K2-only in the sandbox for now.

Even if it works, it is a local search operator (one-token counterfactuals), not 'truly new ways of thinking'. It re-weights what the model can already say, which matches the GFlowNet-style re-sharing goal. It will not invent a new tool or reframe the problem the way FLIP/BORROW try to. If more than 70% of wins are act/ask flips, record that, and say plainly that it overlaps with FLIP's collapse.
attack.fair_baseline: R+ with generated tokens matched: it sees the same 2 failed transcripts with 'try a different approach' and gets extra tries until generated tokens match the DF arm (cap 24), with tries-matched and wall-clock-matched also reported. Two fork controls with the same budget and the same 16-fork, 3-per-window rules: (1) DF-ent: forced runner-up at the highest-entropy decision tokens, the forking-token view from 2506.01939. (2) DF-loc: the same confident positions as DF0, but the model resamples at temp 0.7 from the fork with no forcing (a PivoARL-like local restart without reflection). DF-randdec (random decision tokens of the same types, no confidence filter) replaces the current DF-rand. All arms run on the same HARD-test task ids with the same seeds, and results are compared per task.
attack.likely_effect: SHOWN (puzzle model only): greedy decoding is a bottleneck there (search finds fits for about 36 of 205 pool questions by night 4 while greedy first-try stays near 0), and 'learn the find' methods (hindsight relabel, composition) failed. SUGGESTED: on Reach-1 HARD tasks, forcing runner-up tokens at decision points probably cracks a few tasks that R+ does not, because R+'s rewrites tend to fall back onto the same plan, and a forced token is a stronger jolt than a 'try something different' instruction. Expect a small gap (0-3 tasks) at matched tokens, most of it act/ask and tool-choice flips. SUGGESTED: the 'confident points hide assumptions' story is a coin flip against DF-ent and DF-loc. Under sampling, the chosen token at most positions looks confident, so confidence may just be a proxy for 'decision token'. UNTESTED: that the probe learns which confidences to doubt (not enough data yet). UNTESTED and likely to fail as written: one night of fork-DPO turning cracks into greedy first-try success on new tasks. It will probably pass only on the trained tasks, through memorisation.
attack.improved_test:
DF-1' (K2 only, Reach-1 sandbox, one change at a time, pass marks fixed now). Keep the small card/puzzle results separate; they motivate the test but are not evidence for it.

STEP 0, offline, CPU only, no GPU (gate). Run one teacher-forced pass over the existing HARD failure transcripts and the 270 paused episodes. For each task, count decision-token candidates with p1 >= 0.9 and p2 >= 0.005 that survive the span-completion filter (the forced token must decode to a different tool name, argument value or act/ask choice). Also run the replay-equality hash check. GATE: at least 8 distinct forks per task on at least 70% of HARD tasks, and 100% replay equality. If either fails, stop. The mechanism cannot fill its budget, or the world cannot be rebuilt.

STEP 1, cracking (5070 Ti after 14:00Z Oct 26, or the second Kaggle account). Size the shared HARD screen so HARD-test has at least 40 tasks. Arms at temp 0.7, all generated-token-matched to DF0, 16 forks each: R+ (extra tries up to cap 24), DF0 (confident forks, forced runner-up), DF-ent (high-entropy decision forks, forced runner-up), DF-loc (DF0's positions, no forcing, resample), DF-randdec (random decision tokens, forced runner-up). No probe arm.
PASS (fixed): P1 DF0 cracks >= 5 of HARD-test. P2 DF0 − R+ >= 3, with only-DF0 vs only-R+ one-sided sign test p <= 0.1. P3 DF0 − max(DF-ent, DF-loc, DF-randdec) >= 2. P4 each win replays >= 2/3 from its fork.
PROVED WRONG: DF0 <= R+ means forks add nothing over retries that see failures. DF0 <= DF-loc means the forced token does not matter, only the restart point does. DF0 <= DF-ent means the 'confident, not uncertain' story is false, and the arm reduces to the known forking-token idea. A gap of 1-2 is inconclusive: run seed 2 once, then decide. Report wins by fork type and flag the result if over 70% are act/ask flips.

STEP 2, night, only if P1-P3 pass. Train fork-DPO (LoRA, beta 0.1, nightly KL anchor) only on pairs from HARD-train cracks. Evaluate greedy first-try on (a) HARD-test tasks that DF0 cracked but that were never trained on, (b) the trained HARD-train tasks, reported separately as the memorisation ceiling, and (c) the 100 held-out tasks.
PASS: (a) at least 3 HARD-test tasks newly solved by greedy (base about 0), and (c) a drop of no more than 2 points (paired McNemar).
PROVED WRONG: (b) high but (a) about 0. That is memorisation, consistent with the earlier hindsight-relabel failure, and it means the habit claim fails.

STEP 3, only after at least 30 positive fork outcomes. Fit the probe on HARD-train outcomes. It must beat the log p2 + type heuristic on held-out AUC by at least 0.05 before any crack-based arm is run.

Cost: Step 0 takes CPU-minutes on the Mac. Step 1 is about 5 arms × 40 tasks × 16 forks × about 300 tokens, plus R+, under 2 GPU-hours on the 5070 Ti. Step 2 takes under 30 minutes. No API and no Vast needed.

Plain-language summary for Ben: when the assistant fails, find the spots where it was 'pretty sure but not totally sure' about a choice, make it take its second choice there, and see if that rescues the task. The fair test is whether this beats just letting it retry with the failures in view, and whether those 'pretty sure' spots beat 'unsure' spots or a plain restart from the same place. Only then do we check whether one night of training makes it get these right on its first try, on tasks it was not trained on.

candidates.name: Set-Credit Reframer: a learned creative LoRA that writes the reframe that adds a solve the rest of the set would miss
candidates.one_line: Train a small 'reframer' LoRA on the same 3.7B to write 8 short problem reframes for a stuck task. Each reframe is credited by how many solves it adds that the other 7 do not cover (leave-one-out marginal pass@set), with the worker frozen. Reframes from Claude and the 35B enter as off-policy candidates scored by the worker's real checks, never copied. Exploration is trained to complement, not to be likely or merely rare.
candidates.mechanism:
WHAT IS TRAINED: only a creative LoRA (rank 16, attention+MLP) on K2-3.7B, switched in on the same weights. Input: task request + 2 failed transcripts (the R+ block). Output: 8 numbered reframes, each ≤40 tokens ('Assume the file is in Archive, not Inbox; search there first'). WORKER: the same base with the normal assistant adapter, frozen in the test. It runs the episode with one reframe added through the existing extra-block path (to confirm in the Reach-1 code, which is not in this checkout).
SCORING (night, sandbox): for a stuck training task, set S = 8 reframes, with 2 worker runs each (16 episodes, the R+×16 budget). p_i = reframe i's success fraction. V(S) = 1 − Π(1 − p_i). Credit c_i = V(S) − V(S∖i). A reframe that duplicates another's idea gets about 0 even if it succeeds, and one that never works gets 0. This is the step past FlowRL, which matches each sample to its reward independently and so keeps many copies of one good mode.
OFF-POLICY SOURCES (from Reframe-Flow): up to 8 of the 16 candidates per task come from Claude Batches (16 reframes per task, about 1 cent) or from the 35B tier at night. They are scored by the same worker runs, so a teacher reframe that does not work is pushed down.
UPDATE (no on-policy RL; single-try check RL failed at 1.7B): nightly DPO, beta 0.1, KL anchor, about 300 pairs. Pair type 1: chosen = highest-credit reframe, rejected = zero-credit 'lazy duplicate' (highest ROUGE-L to an earlier reframe in the set). Pair type 2: chosen = a credited reframe, rejected = the reframe whose worker transcripts were nearest to the failed ones (move away from what failed). Variant for later: a trajectory-balance loss with an in-batch log Z on reframe tokens, R = (0.02+s)². Tasks where all 8 scored 0 give no pairs and are rerun the next night with the new adapter.
DAY (serve): stuck trigger, then swap in the reframer, write 8 reframes in one call (about 350 tokens), and run up to 8 sandbox branches with the worker. A reframe that wins and replays becomes a card candidate; one that wins on 3 or more tasks is promoted.
candidates.why_fantastic: Every earlier arm decides HOW to explore by hand (the FLIP template, BORROW by word overlap, a novelty bonus). This makes the exploration policy itself the thing that improves each night, trained on the only quantity that matters when stuck: does this idea crack the task when the others don't? It is the first trained version of Ben's 'change the problem' idea, with a causal reward, and it puts the diversity on the question rather than the answer. The leave-one-out set reward needs no judge, embedding or partition network; it comes straight from deterministic checks. Claude and the 35B become idea sources whose ideas must pass the small worker's own checks. Reframes are short text, so wins are already readable cards, which bridges cards and weights without hindsight relabel.
candidates.why_new: FlowRL, GFlowNet and GFlowRL match per-sample reward. DARLING and uniqueness-aware RL multiply quality by a diversity score judged by an LLM or an embedding. Pass@k training spreads set credit evenly. None credits a sample by its counterfactual marginal contribution to set success, which counts a correct duplicate as 0. Here the trained policy is a separate hint writer acting on a frozen worker, not the solver. Explorer-E1 trains the solver with a novelty bonus. G-Zero's hint-delta is a predictive-shift reward for non-verifiable text. FLIP and BORROW are untrained prompting. Off-policy teacher reframes scored by the worker are not SFT on teacher hints.
candidates.k2_test:
PCR-1, shared K2 screen with STUCK = 0/32. Split STUCK by scenario: 60% TRAIN-STUCK, 40% TEST-HARD with no scenario overlap. If TEST-HARD < 15, use the 1-2/32 tasks as the pre-declared secondary set. 3 training nights on TRAIN-STUCK.
ARMS on TEST-HARD, 16 worker episodes each, the same R+ block, reframe-writing tokens charged to the reframer arms and other arms topped up with R+ tries to within 5%: R+. P0 (untrained creative prompt, 8×2). PCR (trained, 8×2). EQ (equal-compute control: the worker gets the same GPU time as rejection-sampling SFT on its TRAIN-STUCK wins, then R+×16). Ablation SC: the same DPO with plain success-credit (chosen = any successful reframe). Ceiling only, not servable: C = Claude reframes at test time.
PASS (fixed): P1 PCR ≥ max(R+, EQ) + 4 tasks, McNemar p<0.05. P2 PCR − P0 ≥ 3. P3 train-side cracks rise over nights (night 3 > night 1 by ≥3). P4 wins replay ≥2/3 with the same reframe, and a shuffled reframe from another task drops the replay rate by ≥50%.
PROVED WRONG: PCR ≤ P0 + 1, or PCR ≤ R+, or PCR ≤ EQ. Set credit is proved useless if PCR and SC are within 1 task (drop it). Gaps of 2-3 are inconclusive: seed 2. If over 60% of winning reframes are ask-vs-act flips and P0 shows the same share, report it as a sandbox artifact.
candidates.mac_fit: One K2 q4 (about 2.6 GB) plus two LoRA adapters (about 30 MB each) with mlx_lm adapter swap. The reframe call is about 350 tokens, and the branches are about 300 tokens each. It also runs on the 8 GB M2. Nightly DPO on about 300 short pairs at rank 16 takes about 20-30 min on the M1 Pro with mlx_lm.lora, or runs on the PC.
candidates.test_cost: 5070 Ti, vLLM: screen about 1.5 h (shared), 3 nights × about 60 tasks × 16 ≈ 2,900 episodes (about 1 h) plus 3 DPO runs of about 10 min, eval about 1,600 episodes plus replays (about 40 min), EQ SFT about 20 min, SC ablation about 30 min. About 4.5-5.5 GPU-hours, or 2 sessions on the second Kaggle account. Claude Batches for off-policy reframes and the C arm: under $3.

fatal_flaws: The credit formula zeroes correct, different ideas (shown, by arithmetic). Within one task the set has only one thing to cover: the task is solved or it isn't. If two reframes with different ideas each succeed 2/2, then V(S)=1, V(S minus i)=1, and both get credit 0. So the leave-one-out credit doesn't reward 'a solve the others would miss'. It penalises any success that isn't unique, whatever the idea behind it. The same thing happens at p=1/2: two half-working reframes get 0.25 each instead of 0.5. The candidate's own phrase, 'adds solves the rest of the set would miss', only makes sense across several tasks, and the formula works on a single task. On the tasks where the signal is richest (several reframes crack it), the policy would be pushed toward having exactly one reframe that works. That is the opposite of the reliability that card promotion and replay (P4) need. This has to be redefined before any run, or the PCR vs SC comparison measures a broken credit rule and not the idea of set credit.

The training signal will probably be too scarce (suggested). STUCK is defined as 0/32 or 0/64 plain tries. Each reframe gets 2 worker runs, so p_i can only be 0, 0.5 or 1, and in most sets all 8 will be 0. That gives no pairs. Reaching about 300 DPO pairs a night needs roughly 100 or more cracked task-sets out of about 60 TRAIN-STUCK tasks, and that can't happen unless untrained reframes already crack a large share. Nothing so far shows that untrained FLIP/BORROW-style reframes crack these tasks at all: X vs R+ is paused at 270 episodes with no verdict. So the pool may have nothing for training to learn from.
fixable_flaws: Redefine the credit over a cluster of tasks (fix for fatal flaw 1). Group TRAIN-STUCK into scenario clusters of 4-6 tasks. Let S be the 8 reframes, each applied across the cluster. Coverage is the number of tasks in the cluster solved by at least one reframe, and c_i is coverage(S) minus coverage(S minus i). A second option is PKPO's unbiased leave-one-out pass@k estimator (2505.15201) with at least 4 runs per reframe. Either way, give the credit a reliability floor: a reframe that succeeds 2/2 on a task no other reframe covers beats one that succeeds 1/2.

Pair type 1 brings back surface diversity. The rejected item is picked by ROUGE-L similarity to an earlier reframe, and that reframe may itself have succeeded (credit 0 only because it was a duplicate). DPO would then learn 'don't repeat wording' and push down ideas that work, which is the embedding/novelty-bonus style of exploration the candidate says it moves past (suggested). Fix: rejected = zero-credit and zero-success only, with ROUGE used only to break ties.

The claim that teacher reframes are 'never copied' is false as written (shown). When a Claude or 35B reframe is the chosen side of a DPO pair, its likelihood under the reframer goes up, which is imitation, filtered by the worker's checks. That is still a fine design, but the simpler baseline it implies is missing: RFT-reframer, i.e. SFT the reframer on worker-verified reframes from the same pool, with the same number of examples. Without it, any PCR gain may be plain distillation of worker-verified teacher ideas.

2 runs per reframe is too few to estimate credit (suggested). Measure the noise before training: replicate the 2-run scoring twice on the same sets and report the split-half rank correlation of c_i. If it is below 0.4, use 4 runs per reframe with 4 reframes, which stays at 16 episodes.

The test is likely underpowered (suggested). TEST-HARD may have only 15-40 tasks. Clearing +4 tasks over both R+ and EQ with McNemar p<0.05 needs about 6 or more discordant pairs in one direction. Fix the seed count (2) and the task count in advance, and report pass@16 with bootstrap intervals rather than counting on a single McNemar test.

The worker's sampling temperature isn't stated. At greedy decoding, the 2 runs per reframe are identical. Earlier puzzle results show greedy decoding is a bottleneck, so fix one temperature for all arms in advance.

The extra-block injection path is assumed to exist in Reach-1, but that code isn't in this checkout (untested). Confirm it, and confirm that the R+ arm and the reframer arms see the same failed-try block.

Novelty claim (shown, from the prior-art search): the claim must be narrowed. PKPO already does leave-one-out pass@k credit, and HiLL already trains a hinter on failed rollouts. Read 2608.27507 before making any claim. The 'Reframe-Flow' citation has no source and should be removed or given one.

candidates.name: Impasse Forge: break the route that worked, on purpose, so the creative mode practises getting unstuck where a way out is certified
candidates.one_line: Each night, take solved sandbox tasks and block the exact step that made them work (that tool errors, the file moved, the argument form rejected, the info missing), certify that a detour still passes the checks, and keep only blocks the plain model now fails. Train the creative mode by DPO on these certified impasses, with 'pushed on the wall again' as the negative, and test whether the skill transfers to naturally HARD tasks.
candidates.mechanism:
WHY: real stuck tasks are rare and usually unsolved, so an explorer gets almost no positive signal (HARD = 0/64 gives empty pairs). Forging makes stuck states that are known to be solvable, in quantity, from the model's own wins.
FORGE (night, sandbox only; a wrapper around the world's tool-call function): for each plain-solved task, find the load-bearing step by ablation, the first tool call whose removal makes a replay fail. Apply one of 4 typed BLOCKS: (a) that tool returns 'unavailable'; (b) the target item is moved or renamed; (c) the argument form used (date, name, id format) is rejected and needs another form; (d) the expected info is absent, so the right move is to ask. CERTIFY that a detour exists: either the base model within 32 R+ tries, or one Claude Batches trajectory that passes the same end-state checks when run in the blocked world. Claude detours are never trained on; they only certify. KEEP the impasse only if it is certified and the plain worker fails it ≥7/8.
TRAIN: the creative adapter writes up to 8 'approach' lines per impasse, with 1 worker try each. DPO pairs: chosen = an approach whose worker episode passed the checks; rejected = an approach in the same set that repeated the blocked route (detected mechanically: it calls the blocked tool or searches the old location). Block types are balanced at 25% each. KL anchor, beta 0.1.
CURRICULUM: impasses the mode solves ≥4/8 are retired, and blocks are then stacked (2 on one task) so difficulty keeps pace. Today's real wins feed tomorrow's forge, so the set tracks Ben's actual work.
DAY: an ordinary creative call (same trigger, adapter and branches), with nothing extra at serve time. COMBINATION NOTE: if both this and the Set-Credit Reframer pass, forged impasses can be the reframer's training tasks; run them separately first.
candidates.why_fantastic: It turns the scarcest thing, examples of getting unstuck, into something the system makes every night, with ground truth, from its own successes. That trains exactly the skill the creative mode needs: when the normal route is blocked, find another and stop retrying the wall. Every positive passed deterministic end-state checks in the blocked world, so it cannot be gamed by narration. The typed blocks say which kind of detour improved, which is directly useful for designing cards. If it transfers, the assistant gets better at recovering from new failures every night without Ben having to fail first.
candidates.why_new: Random dream school made puzzles from nothing with no certified answer. Forge edits real solved tasks and requires a checked detour before training. Hindsight relabel (AgentHER, ECHO) changes the goal to fit what happened, while Forge keeps the goal and breaks the route. Fission-GRPO and error-recovery retries inject random tool errors into the solver. Forge targets the load-bearing step found by ablation, certifies solvability, retires and stacks blocks as a curriculum, and trains a separate exploration mode with 'repeated the wall' negatives. Absolute Zero and R-Zero generate problems by difficulty, not by a blocked known route. Nothing queued makes certified impasses from wins.
candidates.k2_test:
FORGE-1, K2-3.7B, temp 0.7, 6 turns, shared screen. DATA: forged impasses from plain-solved (≥1/8) tasks in TRAIN scenarios (target 300 kept). TEST-HARD = natural 0/32 tasks in held-out scenarios. FORGE-HELDOUT = 60 forged impasses from TEST scenarios (a sanity check that training worked at all).
ARMS on TEST-HARD (16 worker episodes, same R+ block, matched tokens): R+. P0 (untrained creative approaches 8×2). FG (adapter after 2 forge nights, 8×2). EQ-SOLVER (the same impasses and episode budget spent on worker SFT on its own detour wins, then R+×16: separates 'learned to explore' from 'learned these fixes'). EQ-RANDBLOCK (the same creative training on random tool-error worlds, Fission-style: a control for the forge design).
PASS (fixed): P1 FG ≥ FORGE-HELDOUT base + 15 points. P2 (the real one) FG ≥ max(R+, EQ-SOLVER) + 4 TEST-HARD tasks, McNemar p<0.05. P3 FG − EQ-RANDBLOCK ≥ 2. P4 FG's repeated-the-wall rate on TEST-HARD drops ≥30% relative to R+ (mechanism check). Wins replay ≥2/3.
PROVED WRONG: P1 met but FG ≤ R+ + 1 on TEST-HARD (forge-specific skill, no transfer: stop). FG ≤ EQ-SOLVER (explore-training is worse than solver training on the same data). P1 failing (the signal is too weak at 3.7B). Gaps of 2-3 are inconclusive: seed 2. Per-block-type counts are reported, not deciding.
candidates.mac_fit: Serve time is a normal creative call: K2 q4 plus one adapter of about 30 MB. The heavy forge (about 100 tasks × 16 episodes) runs on the PC or Kaggle. The Mac nightly version forges only today's 10-30 real wins, about 1-2 h with mlx_lm, which fits the one capped job. DPO on about 200 pairs takes about 20 min.

prior.notes: Prior-art verdict: partly-new. The pieces have prior art: error-recovery training (Fission-GRPO, 2601.15625, ACL 2026), tool-failure benchmarks with injected faults (ToolMaze, 2606.05806), hindsight relabeling of failed agent runs into DPO data (AgentHER 2603.21357; ECHO 2510.10304; HSL 2607.04235), and synthetic task curricula from exploration (AutoPlay 2509.25047, DreamGym 2511.03773, Self-Challenging 2506.01716, Envs-FORGE 2608.14312). Not found in 8 searches or 0 page fetches: any paper that finds a load-bearing tool call by ablation and blocks it; any certification that a detour passes the end-state checks (base-model tries or one Batches trajectory); DPO negatives defined as 'calls the blocked tool or searches the old location'; a curriculum that stacks blocks after the mode solves an impasse ≥4/8. The combination is the new part. Claim-check against the candidate text: (1) it says Fission-GRPO injects 'random tool errors into the solver'. The paper instead adds feedback from a fine-tuned error simulator to failed trajectories and resamples recovery rollouts, so 'random' is a loose description and should be corrected before this is cited. (2) 'Hindsight relabel changes the goal': AgentHER relabels the goal with the trajectory kept, and ECHO rewrites both goal and steps, so the contrast is roughly right for AgentHER but needs the ECHO nuance. (3) Absolute Zero and R-Zero were named in the candidate but not checked here. known-ids status: 2601.15625 and 2603.21357 are already in /mnt/project-files/research/sweep-2026/known-ids.txt (count 1 each), so they were seen in an earlier sweep. 2601.00747 (reasoning-creativity trade-off, which treats DPO and GRPO as special cases of one loss) is also already listed. Not listed, so new to the sweep: 2606.05806, 2510.10304, 2607.04235, 2509.25047, 2511.03773, 2506.01716, 2512.19682, 2608.14312, 2511.06101, 2608.28363, 2608.19197, 2606.31270 (inference-time computer-use learning from failure, not training). Risk notes for the reviewer: Fission-GRPO code is not public, so a head-to-head is not possible yet; the K2 test's control arms (EQ-RANDBLOCK) effectively reproduce Fission-style training, so the forge's novelty claim rests on P3 and P4. Suggested follow-up searches, not run: 'Absolute Zero' and 'R-Zero' for self-play task generation, and 'load-bearing step ablation agent trajectory' for ablation-based failure localization.

fatal_flaws: The skill it trains may not be the skill HARD tasks need (suggested, not yet measured). Forged impasses come from tasks the plain model already solves (at least 1/8), with one known route blocked. Natural HARD tasks are 0/64, and most likely fail because of a capability or understanding gap (a misread goal, a missing multi-step plan, unknown tool semantics), not because one good route hits a wall. If few HARD failures look like 'a good route hit a wall', P2 cannot pass however well the forge works. Nobody has measured this failure mix yet (untested), and the whole test depends on it.

P2 as written cannot be reached. A gain of +4 tasks with McNemar p<0.05 needs at least 6 tasks where only one arm wins, all going FG's way (exact two-sided 6-0 gives p=0.031, while 4-0 gives p=0.125). So '+4 and p<0.05' contradicts itself unless TEST-HARD is large, and its size is not stated. Shown (arithmetic). The pass mark must be fixed against the real size of TEST-HARD before the run, or the result will be read after the fact.
fixable_flaws: P4 has no definition on TEST-HARD. 'Repeated the wall' is detected by calling the blocked tool or searching the old location, but natural tasks have no known wall. Redefine it for every set: the same failing tool and argument signature called 2 or more times after an error.
Block (d), 'info missing, so ask', cannot be certified in a sandbox that only checks end states and has no simulated user. Either add a scripted user reply or drop (d) and rebalance to 3 types.

Ablation will mostly pick the final writing call, so most blocks turn into type (a). The 25% balance will then be forced onto rare or odd cases. Report how blocks are naturally spread before balancing (suggested).

There is a shortcut risk. Forged errors use fixed text ('unavailable', 'rejected format'), so the adapter can learn 'keyword means switch tool' without learning to explore. Vary the error wording, and include about 20% decoy blocks that are temporary, where retrying the same call is correct. Otherwise 'never repeat' becomes a harmful reflex in real use, where a retry is often the right move.

The keep filter (plain model fails 7/8 or more, but R+ certifies within 32 tries) means R+ already solves every kept impasse. So P1 against the base model is too easy. Score P1 against R+ on FORGE-HELDOUT, not against the plain base.

The design rests on an unfinished experiment. Reach-1 R+ vs X is paused at 270 episodes, so nobody yet knows whether creative 'approach lines' beat R+ at all (P0 vs R+). Finish it, or run P0 vs R+ on the forge set, before paying for training.

The novelty text misdescribes Fission-GRPO: it uses a fine-tuned error simulator, not 'random' errors. Also, EQ-RANDBLOCK is effectively the Fission-style training, so the novelty claim rests entirely on P3. Gaps of 2 tasks will be noise. Set P3 as an advance-fixed margin with a seed-2 rule.

The puzzle model's history counts against it (suggested). Synthetic curricula (dream school), hindsight relabel and composition all failed there. Only more sleep nights helped. The forge is another kind of synthetic task generation, so the bar to keep it should be high.
attack.fair_baseline: Equal compute and matched tokens on TEST-HARD: (1) R+ with 16 tries that see earlier failures. (2) PROMPT-DETOUR: R+ plus a fixed, untrained instruction ('state what the last error rules out; pick a different tool, argument form or source; never resend a call that failed'). This costs nothing and is the baseline most likely to match FG. (3) EQ-SOLVER: same impasses and training budget, spent on worker SFT on its own detour wins. (4) EQ-RANDBLOCK: Fission-style training on random tool-error worlds. (5) Extra-sleep: the same GPU-hours spent on ordinary nightly LoRA nights, since more sleep is the only thing that has reliably helped so far. FG must beat the best of these.
attack.likely_effect: Shown: nothing yet; there are no forge runs. Suggested: FG will clearly beat the base on FORGE-HELDOUT (P1 likely passes). It will cut repeated identical failing calls on real logs, which helps Ben in daily use. On natural 0/32 TEST-HARD tasks it will probably gain 0-2 tasks over R+ and PROMPT-DETOUR, which is inconclusive. The gain will be largest on HARD tasks whose traces show a repeated failing call. Untested: whether HARD failures are mostly route blocks, whether the DPO lift survives the KL anchor at 3.7B, and whether the 'never repeat' rule hurts tasks where retrying is correct.
attack.improved_test:
Run it in stages, with each pass mark fixed before that stage starts. Do not use the village model; this is a card-scale test only.

STAGE 0, failure triage (no GPU, about $2 of Claude Batches, Haiku). Take the existing failed traces on Reach-1 HARD tasks, 8 per task. A fixed rubric labels each trace: ROUTE-BLOCKED (the same failing call or source repeated), GOAL-MISREAD, PLAN-MISSING, or OTHER. Check 30 of the labels by hand. GO only if ROUTE-BLOCKED is the main failure in at least 30% of HARD tasks. If not, transfer has nowhere to happen: stop, or retarget the forge at the dominant failure type.

STAGE 1, no training (PC, about 1 h). Finish Reach-1 R+ vs X, or run P0 vs R+ vs PROMPT-DETOUR on 100 forged impasses. Report how blocks naturally spread across the types. GO only if P0 or PROMPT-DETOUR is at least R+ minus 2 points. If untrained approach lines are much worse, the creative-call format itself is the problem.

STAGE 2, training. One change from the base plan: drop block (d), and add varied error wording plus 20% decoys that are temporary errors, where retrying is correct. Arms on TEST-HARD-ROUTE: R+, PROMPT-DETOUR, EQ-SOLVER, EQ-RANDBLOCK, EXTRA-SLEEP and FG, all with matched tokens and 16 episodes. TEST-HARD-ROUTE is the Stage-0 ROUTE-BLOCKED subset of held-out HARD, at least 40 tasks, plus all of TEST-HARD reported separately.
Pass marks:
- P1: FG ≥ R+ + 10 points on FORGE-HELDOUT.
- P2: FG − max(other arms) ≥ k tasks on TEST-HARD-ROUTE, where k is the smallest McNemar-significant margin for that n, computed and written down before the run.
- P3: FG − EQ-RANDBLOCK ≥ 3.
- P4: 30% or larger relative drop in repeated identical failing calls, where 'repeated' means the same failing call signature 2 or more times after an error.
- P5 (harm check): FG's success on decoy and normal non-HARD tasks drops by no more than 2 points against the base.
- Wins must replay at least 2/3.

Proved wrong if:
- P1 passes but FG ≤ PROMPT-DETOUR + 1 on TEST-HARD-ROUTE (a prompt is enough, so don't train).
- FG ≤ EQ-SOLVER or ≤ EXTRA-SLEEP (training a separate explore mode is the wrong use of nightly compute).
- P5 fails (it learned a reflex that hurts normal tasks).

A gap of 1 to k−1 tasks runs seed 2 only once. Real-use check after a pass: for 2 weeks, log on the Mac how often the nightly forge adapter ends stuck episodes in Ben's own logs, compared with the R+ trigger alone.

Plain summary for Ben: the idea is to practise getting unstuck by deliberately breaking things that already worked. Before building it, check that your hard tasks actually fail because a route is blocked. Then check that a plain written hint like 'don't repeat the failed step' isn't already just as good.

candidates.name: Latent Escape: learned fail-to-win activation directions as branches, then an overnight checker-guided search in their span
candidates.one_line: Each night, mine the hidden-state directions that separated the model's own winning tries from its failed tries on the same tasks, and orthogonalise them into a small escape basis. When stuck, run each branch near-greedy under a different direction, so branches differ in where the model thinks from rather than in sampling noise. For tasks still stuck overnight, run an evolution-strategies search over combinations of those directions, scored by partial checks and decoded greedily so any find replays exactly.
candidates.mechanism:
STORED: a basis E of 16 unit vectors at one middle layer L of K2-3.7B (L chosen once on train tasks from about 40/50/60% depth), each with a strength alpha_k, a win count, and an optional strategy label. About 200 KB. Per-task finds: a 16-number coefficient vector c, about 100 bytes.
NIGHT BUILD (forward passes only): (1) Take mixed tasks, some tries winning and some failing (screen 1-7/8, and in deployment day logs). (2) Re-run their transcripts through the current weights (after that night's LoRA) and record h_L averaged over the turn-1 assistant tokens (plan plus first tool call). (3) delta_t = mean(h|win) − mean(h|fail), minus the across-task mean, so that 'success in general' is not one shared direction. (4) k-means (k=16) on the normalised deltas, then Gram-Schmidt. (5) alpha = the largest scale at which ≥90% of steered turns still emit valid tool-call JSON on 20 easy tasks. Optional, report-only: Claude Batches labels each cluster's winning transcripts with a strategy name (under $2), so a direction becomes a readable card ('inspect state before acting'). Rebuild after every nightly LoRA.
DAY (stuck mode, MENU): with the same R+ block and no extra prompt tokens, branch i adds alpha·||h_L||·e_i at layer L on every generated token of turn 1 (all turns if train tasks favour it), decoding at temp 0.3. Use the top 8 directions by win count, 2 tries each.
NIGHT SEARCH (for tasks still stuck, from Latent Incubation): antithetic ES over c ∈ R^16 with the steering vector Σ c_k e_k: population 8, 4 generations, sigma tuned on train tasks, every candidate decoded GREEDILY. Fitness = 1 for strict success; otherwise 0.5 × the fraction of end-state checks passed, gated so that a fake done-claim or no tool call on a tool task scores 0, plus 0.1 if its tool-call sequence differs from every failed transcript. A winning c is stored as a latent card for that task type and replays exactly.
WEIGHTS: a direction or c that wins on 3 or more tasks feeds steered transcripts as chosen examples into the planned DPO/KTO pairs (distillation, Ben's recurring-only rule). Directions with 0 wins in 14 days are retired.
candidates.why_fantastic: It produces new behaviour from structure the model cannot put into words. FLIP only reaches assumptions the model can name, and its opposites collapse onto ask-vs-act. These directions come from the model's own internal fail-to-win differences on Ben's tasks, so they can encode shifts with no short verbal form, which suits a 3.7B that reframes poorly in words. Tries cost no context tokens, which matters on the 8 GB tier. Steered near-greedy branches, and the greedy ES finds, attack the measured greedy bottleneck directly: the thing found is itself a greedy-decodable configuration, so it is reproducible by construction. The ES stage gives the search a gradient (partial checks) on tasks where every plain try is 0. The basis grows from real use: the more fail-then-fix episodes a day produces, the richer the escape menu.
candidates.why_new: CAA and ITI build one direction from human-labelled behaviour pairs. STARS pushes concurrent runs apart with no notion of success. Noise steering is random. Black-Box Tuning runs CMA-ES over a random-projection soft-prompt subspace for labelled classification. None mines a menu of directions from the model's own same-task win/fail pairs, uses them as budget-matched branches in a tool sandbox against random-direction and temperature controls, and then searches their span per stuck task overnight with a checker as the only fitness and greedy decoding for exact replay. Nothing queued (FLIP, BORROW, Explorer-E1/E2 idea dial, blocks, mashups, decoding change) touches activations. E2 trains a latent input, while this trains nothing.
candidates.k2_test:
ESC-1, shared K2 screen, HARD split by scenario. E is built only from TRAIN-split mixed tasks; HARD is never used to build E. GATE (fixed before the HARD run): build E on half A of the mixed train tasks and apply it to failed-prefix situations from half B. If best-of-16 steered success does not beat plain 16-try resampling on half B by ≥5 points, stop and report that the directions do not generalise.
STAGE 1 ARMS on held-out HARD, 16 episodes each, the same R+ block and turns: R+ (temp 0.7). R+hot (temp 1.0: more randomness alone). RAND (8 random orthogonal vectors, same layer and norms, temp 0.3, 2 each: any perturbation). ESC (learned bank, temp 0.3, 2 each). PASS: ESC cracks ≥5; ESC − max(R+, R+hot) ≥ 3 with only-ESC ≥ 2× (McNemar); ESC − RAND ≥ 2; each win replays ≥2/3 with the same direction. PROVED WRONG: ESC ≤ RAND or ESC ≤ R+; also killed if >25% of ESC episodes fail the tool-call format check.
STAGE 2 (run only if stage 1 is not proved wrong; a separate change): on HARD tasks that ESC did not crack, 32 greedy episodes each: ES (4×8 over c), RANDC (32 random c, same sigma, greedy, no updates), R+32. PASS: ES − RANDC ≥ 2 and ES − R+32 ≥ 2. PROVED WRONG: ES ≤ RANDC. Gaps of 1-2 are inconclusive: seed 2. Report per-direction win counts and the ask-vs-act share. Pre-registered transfer check, not deciding: rebuild E on the Mac q4 model and replay GPU wins there, requiring ≥70% of the same first-action changes before claiming the Mac result.
candidates.mac_fit: Serving needs one residual add at layer L (a few-line wrapper on one decoder layer in the mlx_lm K2 model file; plain attention makes it simple). The basis is under 1 MB, with no extra prompt or memory, so it runs on the 8 GB M2. The nightly build is forward passes plus k-means, minutes on the GPU or about 1-2 h on the Mac for about 2,000 transcripts. Night ES for about 20 stuck tasks × 32 greedy episodes is about 0.5M tokens, roughly 1-1.5 h batched on the M1 Pro. Risks: fp16-built directions may act differently on q4 (hence the transfer check, and production builds on the Mac q4 model), and the Gated DeltaNet 35B tier needs its own check.
candidates.test_cost: About 3-4 GPU-hours on the 5070 Ti beyond the shared screen: activation extraction about 0.3 h, alpha grid about 0.4 h, gate about 0.5 h, stage-1 arms about 1.5 h, stage 2 about 1 h (HF transformers with a forward hook, batched populations). closest_work.title: COAST: Contrastive Conceptor Activation Steering (May 2026, robotics VLA)
closest_work.overlap: Closest on the core mechanism. Uses a few success and failure rollouts of the same task to find success-critical activation subspaces, then steers hidden states toward them at inference. Training-free. Covers the 'mine win/fail directions from the model's own rollouts' step, but as conceptor subspaces for robot policies, not LLM tool-use tasks, and not as a stored menu of branches or an ES search.

closest_work.overlap: Steers concurrent runs apart with orthogonal additive directions (volume maximisation on the Stiefel manifold). closest_work.overlap: Argues that steering vectors built from contrasts between outcome-labelled representations can encode downstream state visitation rather than the decision that matters, and proposes accumulating activation gradients from scored trajectories instead. Verdict: the parts are not new, but the combination is only partly new. The proposal's 'why_new' claim that nothing mines directions from same-task win/fail pairs is overstated: COAST does this for robot policies with conceptor subspaces. Items the proposal does not cover at all: ES or black-box search over steering coefficients with a checker fitness. I found none in the search results, though GER-steer and Bias-only tuning are nearby. Not verified this session, from memory only: CAA (Rimsky et al. 2023), ITI (Li et al. 2023), RepE (Zou et al. 2023), Black-Box Tuning (Sun et al. 2022), refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024). The proposal's baseline list should cite these.

Concrete implications for the proposal: (a) COAST and PGS together mean the stage-1 gate and the 'delta = win - fail' step need an explicit control against outcome-correlated state visitation, not just a random-direction control. (b) The RAND arm and SPREAD/STARS-style volume-maximising directions are the obvious baselines. Add a STARS arm, since it is the closest training-free diversity method and is cheap to run. (c) Cite COAST as the nearest mechanism and state the robotics-to-LLM difference. (d) The 2609.24066 abstract mentions mid-to-late-layer steering, which supports checking the layer choice. Abstract only, not verified in full.

fatal_flaws: The win-minus-fail direction comes from words the model already wrote, not from where it was thinking. On the same task, win tries and fail tries get the exact same prompt, so h_L at the decision point (the last prompt token) is identical for both. The step-(2) mean over the turn-1 assistant tokens, recomputed with teacher forcing, differs only because the plan and first-tool-call text differ. delta_t therefore encodes 'the text of the winning plan' (tool names, ordering words). This is the outcome-correlated state-visitation problem that Policy Gradient Steering raises, made stronger because there is no pre-decision signal at all. Adding that vector pushes generation toward common surface tokens of winning plans on OTHER tasks. That is BORROW done in activation space with less information. It is not a 'way of thinking with no verbal form'. (suggested; follows directly from how the mechanism is built)

The building data does not match the target. E is mined only from mixed tasks (1-7/8 wins), where the fail-to-win difference is mostly sampling luck between two plans the model can already produce. HARD tasks are 0/64, so the needed behaviour is probably missing from the model, not just under-weighted. The repo's own puzzle results point the same way: picking or relabelling what the model already does (aha/MDL, hindsight, composition) failed, and only more training nights helped. A bank that re-weights existing mixed-task plans is the kind of re-sharing that has not worked here so far. (suggested)

Stage 2 ES probably cannot beat its own RANDC control as designed. Greedy decoding makes fitness piecewise-constant in c: most perturbations give the same token sequence, so antithetic pairs tie and the gradient estimate is mostly zero or noise. With 32 evaluations in 16 dimensions and 4 generations, ES is in practice random search. The 0.1 novelty bonus rewards any different tool sequence, not progress. The expected outcome is ES ≈ RANDC, which is the proposal's own 'proved wrong' result, after about 1 GPU-hour. (suggested; untested)
fixable_flaws: Stored latent cards stop meaning anything the next night. E is rebuilt after every nightly LoRA, so a saved 16-number c refers to a basis that no longer exists, and 'replays exactly' only holds until the next sleep. Fix: store the raw d-dimensional steering vector plus the weights hash, and re-check every card after each LoRA (drop it if replay is below 2/3).

There is no label-permutation control. RAND only shows that 'some perturbation' is not enough. Add PERM: the same pipeline (same tasks, same k-means, same alpha calibration) with win/fail labels shuffled within each task. If ESC ≈ PERM, success labels carry no information and the bank is just structured diversity.

There is no text-equivalent baseline for what the direction actually encodes. Add BORROW-TEXT: put the nearest train task's winning turn-1 plan in context (matched tokens counted against the R+ budget). If ESC is not better than this, the activation route only saves context tokens. That matters for the 8 GB tier but is not 'new thinking'.

STARS/SPREAD-style volume-maximising directions are missing as the training-free diversity baseline (the prior-art note). A cheap stand-in: 8 orthogonal directions taken from the top principal components of turn-1 h_L across all tries, which gives structured but success-blind directions.

The statistics are too small. The arms use 16 episodes each, there is no HARD task count, and the pass mark is 'cracks ≥5'. McNemar with fewer than about 10 discordant pairs cannot reach significance, so the '2×' rule is close to a coin flip. Fix the number of HARD tasks n in advance, report a binomial confidence interval, and plan for 2 seeds from the start instead of 'inconclusive, run seed 2'.

k-means with k=16 on perhaps 100-300 noisy per-task deltas in a 3,000+ dimensional space will mostly cluster noise. Use a cross-validated check instead: hold out tasks and see whether each direction's cosine with held-out deltas beats PERM. Use fewer directions (4-8), or the top singular vectors of the stacked deltas.

Steering every generated turn-1 token at 90% JSON validity still leaves up to 10% broken calls, and R+ has no such cost. Steer only the plan tokens and turn steering off inside the tool-call JSON span. Report invalid-format failures separately.

The 35B Gated DeltaNet tier is not addressed. Its layers are mostly recurrent, so the residual stream at '50% depth' sits between DeltaNet blocks with state carried across tokens, and steering may build up inside the recurrent state. Keep any claim restricted to K2-3.7B.
attack.fair_baseline: Same tasks, same turn count, the same R+ failed-tries block, and matched generated tokens. (1) R+ at temp 0.7 and at temp 1.0, 16 tries. (2) PERM: the label-shuffled bank, built by the same pipeline, temp 0.3, 8×2. (3) BORROW-TEXT: the nearest train task's winning plan in context, with the tokens charged to the budget. (4) PCA-diversity bank (success-blind, STARS stand-in). For stage 2: R+32 and RANDC with the same sigma, plus 'greedy with R+ block + 32 distinct seeds of temp-0.3 prefixes', which also replays exactly if the seed is stored. That last point undercuts the 'reproducible by construction' advantage: any sampled win replays if its RNG seed is stored, so greedy decoding is not the only way to get exact replay.
attack.likely_effect: Untested overall. My prediction (suggested): on half-B mixed tasks, ESC will roughly match BORROW-TEXT and beat RAND by a few points, because it encodes common winning-plan tokens. On HARD (0/64), it will be at or under the R+ baseline (0-2 cracks, inside noise), with ESC ≈ PERM. Stage 2: ES ≈ RANDC, because greedy decoding makes fitness flat. Shown: nothing yet. COAST (robotics) shows win/fail conceptor steering helps when the policy already succeeds sometimes. That supports a mixed-task gain, not a HARD-task gain.
attack.improved_test:

(a) Diagnostic first (forward passes only, about 10 min). For each mixed train task, compute delta at the LAST PROMPT TOKEN and over the turn-1 tokens. Report whether the prompt-token delta is about zero. If it is (expected), say plainly in the write-up that the direction is content-derived. Also report the cosine between each bank direction and the mean embedding of the winning plans' tool-name tokens. If the median |cos| is ≥0.3, the bank is a tool-name nudge.
(b) Build E on half A and evaluate on failed-prefix situations from half B (pre-registered n of tasks ≥60, 16 tries per arm, matched tokens). Arms: R+ (0.7), R+hot (1.0), RAND, PERM (labels shuffled within task, same pipeline), PCA-diversity, BORROW-TEXT, ESC. Steer the plan tokens only.

candidates.name: Prepared Mind: an open-questions board where each new win goes looking for old failures
candidates.one_line: Keep every stuck task on a board, indexed by where it got blocked. Each night, boil every new mixed-outcome task down to the one decisive step that separated its passes from its fails, phrase it as a portable rule, and try that rule on the open questions with a matching blocked-at signature. This reverses BORROW: a solution goes looking for a problem.
candidates.mechanism:
STORED (SQLite or JSON, a few MB). (1) Board: one row per stuck task (0/N plain tries, a repeated tool error, or Ben says it is wrong), holding the request, its 2 earliest failed transcripts, and a BLOCKED-AT signature built only from the transcript, never from check results: last tool called, error class (not found / bad args / permission / empty result / no tool call), the step index where it stalled, tools never called, and asked-vs-acted. (2) Key-move library: one row per decisive move, holding 1-2 imperative sentences with no task-specific names, an UNBLOCKS signature in the same feature space, the source task, and a crack counter.
NIGHT EXTRACTION (the new part): for mixed tasks (1-7 of 8 in the screen; in deployment, request types solved on some days and failed on others), align pass and fail transcripts by normalised tool-call sequence. Find the earliest step that ≥80% of passes contain and ≤20% of fails contain ('list_dir before edit_file', 'search the partial name'). That is a diff, with no model involved. Then one K2 call: 'These 2 passes and 2 fails differ at step k. State the move as a rule that would work on a different job.' UNBLOCKS = the fails' blocked-at features at step k. MATCH: for each board row, rank moves by weighted Jaccard over the features (no embeddings) and run 1 sandbox try for each of the top 4 moves. A crack goes to 3 replays. A move that passes becomes a card candidate for Ben to confirm, and the row is closed.
DAY: when creative mode fires, compute the live failure's blocked-at signature and inject the top 2 matched moves ('A move that unblocked similar stalls: ...'), about 60 tokens.
WEIGHTS (only recurring moves): a move that cracked ≥3 different tasks becomes step-level DPO pairs at the divergence point (shared prefix; chosen = the pass branch at step k, rejected = the fail branch at step k), with the KL anchor. That moves probability at the exact step where greedy goes wrong.
candidates.why_fantastic: Every planned operator starts from the failure at the moment of being stuck, with one context's worth of ideas. Prepared Mind makes every future success a chance to solve every past failure, the way a researcher keeps open questions in mind and notices when an unrelated result answers one (the opportunistic-assimilation account of incubation). It compounds: more days bring more mixed tasks, more moves and more matches, so the board drains. The stored unit is the contrastive decisive step (about 30 tokens), not a whole transcript, so it fits the 8 GB tier and transfers where full transcripts copy the wrong tool names. The same divergence points give step-level training pairs, the precise signal that hindsight and composition lacked.
candidates.why_new: BORROW goes from a failure to the nearest whole solved transcript by word overlap at retry time. This goes from win to failure, stores only the pass-vs-fail decisive step, and matches on structural blocked-at features. Playbook cards are built from wins with no contrast against failures. Queued incubation retries the same miss with no new input. Blocks, DreamCoder, LATM and TroVE store whole programs or tools. PivoARL, Reflective Recovery and ECHO reuse failed prefixes within a task or relabel goals. None keeps a cross-task board of open failures that each new win is pushed against.
candidates.k2_test:
PREP-1 (tool sandbox only). Shared K2 screen with HARD = 0/32 (pre-register this in a new PREREG; Reach-1's is not edited). If HARD < 8, stop and report. Mixed tasks (1-7/8) supply the library for free.
ARMS per HARD task, 16 tries each, with extra-block length matched within 10% by padding with the R+ sentence: R+ (control). K (R+ block + one matched move per try: top 8 by signature, 2 each). KR (R+ block + 8 random library moves: matching vs any short rule). KT (R+ block + the full source transcript for the same 8 matched moves: decisive move vs whole solution; report-only).
PASS (fixed): K cracks ≥4; K − R+ ≥ 3 with only-K ≥ 2× only-R+ (paired); K − KR ≥ 2; each K win replays ≥2/3.
PROVED WRONG: K ≤ R+, or K ≤ KR (matching adds nothing over random rules). Inconclusive between: seed 2. Report how many distinct moves crack anything.
STAGE 2, only if PASS (the drain test): stream the 320 train tasks as 4 'days' of 80, extract and match after each day, and count board closures against a board that gets 4 extra R+ tries per night at the same token cost. Pass: matching closures ≥ 2× R+ closures by day 4.
candidates.mac_fit: Serve time is prompt text only: the signature is computed in Python, matching is Jaccard over a few hundred rows (under 1 ms), and about 60 tokens are injected. K2 q4 is unchanged, so it runs on the 8 GB M2. The night match (about 20 rows × 4 probes × about 2k tokens, about 160k tokens) takes minutes in the Mac's capped mlx job. Step-level DPO is a standard LoRA night step.
candidates.test_cost: Shared screen (about 1-1.5 h on the 5070 Ti alone at 0/32), move extraction negligible, arms about 1,280 episodes plus replays (about 0.7 GPU-hours). About 2-2.5 GPU-hours total on the 5070 Ti (4-6 on a T4), plus about 2 h for the drain stage. No API.
